key_insight: Front-peaked tool–workpiece contact pressure best explains BT-FSW temperature and material flow, including hotter retreating-side temperatures caused by hot material deflecting from the advancing side.
engineering_relevance: Accurate contact-pressure modeling can improve predictions used to optimize heat distribution and material transport in bobbin tool friction stir welding.
method: Developed a fully coupled thermo-mechanical-fluid CFD model.
Compared front-peaked, uniform, and rear-peaked interface contact-pressure models.
Examined temperature fields, plastic deformation zones, and material flow trajectories.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports superior predictive accuracy for the front-peaked model and experimental agreement that the retreating side was hotter than the advancing side, without quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Applicability across other materials, tool geometries, and welding conditions is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Spatial characteristic of temperature distribution and material flow behaviors during bobbin tool friction stir welding: a computational fluid dynamics study
